The 4*pi*r^2 division and spin factor are not literally stated in 12.7, but are pinned by step 12.8's background (U''=-8 pi r rho requires 3D density) and standard atomic physics; verified wrong variants (no 4 pi r^2; spinless 2l+1) both FAIL, so tests are constraining.

First honest expert attempt FAILED 0/3; passes 3/3 (confirmed for all of Z=8,16,6) only after reverse-engineering the author's exact SCF loop/reporting structure via a 12-variant search (see D4 finding). Also heavy: ~150-200 s per test with a reasonable pure-Python Numerov -- exceeds steptest's 120 s default; official harness runs all 3 tests in one script under 1800 s, which fits (~450-600 s) but leaves little headroom for slower-but-correct implementations.

findings.evidence: Prompt only says: 'The mixing ratio between old and new charge densities is 0.5 ... If an integration method is used to solve for the second term in the total energy, i.e. $\int d\vec{r} \rho(\vec{r}) [-\epsilon_H(\vec{r})]$, normalize the result using Simpson's rule.' With the test inputs (tolerance=1e-7, iteration=10) the SCF is NOWHERE NEAR converged at the 10-iteration cap: successive-iterate total energies still oscillate by ~0.5 Ry (it7..it9 band energies -69.996, -70.583, -69.744), so the frozen target encodes one specific unconverged 10th iterate and every unstated loop/reporting choice changes the answer by orders of magnitude more than the pass tolerance (~1.3e-3 Ry via np.allclose rtol on E=-133). Measured on test 1 (Z=8, target E=-133.06806083): 12 reasonable convention combinations [trajectory: mix-from-first-iteration-with-rho_old=0 vs no-mixing-on-first-iteration] x [E2 density: raw new vs mixed] x [E2 potential U: pre-update U used in the eigen-solve vs U recomputed from mixed rho vs U from raw rho] give Etot in {-132.066, -132.564(x2), -133.062, -133.068, -133.572, -134.112, -134.149, -134.152, -134.187(x2), -134.227}; EXACTLY ONE matches: no first-iteration mixing, U updated from mixed density, E2 = -simpson(rho_mix * U_new/(2r) * 4*pi*r^2), returned density = mixed (rho maxdiff 8.2e-8). My first literal-reading implementation (identical except E2 evaluated with the pre-update U that generated the eigenvalues -- an equally defensible double-counting convention) failed all 3 tests: -133.5719 vs -133.0681, 380x the tolerance. Returning the raw (unmixed) final density also fails (maxdiff 0.083 vs target).
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) make the target convention-insensitive by letting the SCF actually converge before the cap (raise iteration to ~60 with mixing 0.5, or loosen tolerance to ~1e-5 and assert only the converged values), since at the fixed point all pairings coincide; or (b) state the loop explicitly in the prompt: 'per iteration: solve bound states with current U; build rho_new and band energy; mix rho = 0.5*rho_old + 0.5*rho_new (no mixing on the first iteration); recompute U from the mixed rho; total_energy = band_energy - simpson(rho * U/(2r) * 4*pi*r^2, x=r_grid); return the mixed density and the last total_energy.'

findings.evidence: Tests pass up_at_0=-1e-10 with step ~ -0.526, so the whole solution has magnitude <= 2.1e-8 -- the same scale as np.allclose's default atol=1e-8. Verified against the frozen targets: an all-zeros array PASSES tests 2 and 3 (max|target| = 1.64e-9 and 7.95e-9 < atol); for test 2, 0.5x, 2x and even sign-NEGATED outputs all pass. Uniform scale errors of +/-10% pass all three tests. Step credit still requires test 1 (max|target|=2.09e-8), which rejects zeros/half/double/negated, so a totally wrong solution is caught, but the suite verifies the integrator only to ~10% amplitude -- e.g. a non-Numerov O(h^2) integrator solving the same ODE would pass, and 2 of 3 test cases are individually vacuous.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate targets with a starting slope that is not absorbed by atol (e.g. up_at_0 = -1e-3 in the 12.2 test calls only), or assert with np.allclose(..., atol=0) / compare the solution normalized to unit max.

overall_assessment: Steps 12.1-12.13 are fair and well-posed: every step passed a first-attempt literal-reading expert implementation (13/14 steps, 39/39 test cases), targets are non-degenerate, and the few unstated conventions (3D density = u^2/(4 pi r^2) with spin degeneracy 2(2l+1); reuse of 12.3's integration conventions in 12.10) are pinned by the surrounding backgrounds and verified to be the only passing readings. The serious defect is 12.14: the test fixes an UNCONVERGED 10th SCF iterate while the prompt leaves the loop/mixing/energy-reporting structure underdetermined -- 12 defensible conventions spread over ~2 Ry against a ~1e-3 Ry tolerance, and only one exact structure (recovered here only by search) passes, so competent solvers will commonly fail this step for non-physics reasons. Secondary: 12.2's targets sit at np.allclose's default atol, making 2 of its 3 test cases individually vacuous. Note for harness operators: 12.14 needs ~150-200 s per test case with a reasonable pure-Python implementation (steptest's 120 s default times out; the official 1800 s is sufficient).
